name: Network Latency
description: High network latency between servers can significantly increase the time it takes for the servers to reach consensus, forcing them to repeatedly ask for coin flips.

name: Server Hardware/Configuration
description: Differences in server hardware (CPU, memory, network bandwidth) or configuration (e.g., buffer size) can influence the coin flip timings and the responsiveness of the servers.

name: Server Load
description: High load on either server can cause increased delays during coin flips, especially if the servers are struggling to process requests.

name: DNS Latency
description: DNS resolution latency can introduce a delay, particularly if the servers are pulling data from different DNS servers.

name: Protocol Overhead
description: The inherent overhead of the consensus protocol itself, including round-trip times for communications, can contribute to latency.

name: Queue Length
description: If the servers have a queue of requests waiting to be processed, this can lead to increased latency during coin flips.

name: Cache Hit Ratio
description: If the servers have a low cache hit ratio, they need to frequently retrieve data from memory, slowing down the process.

name: Time Synchronization
description: Inconsistent or inaccurate time synchronization between servers can introduce delays in the timing of the coin flips.

name: Operating System Latency
description: The operating system running on the servers can have latency that affects the timing of the coin flips.

name: Message Loss
description: Lost messages during the consensus process can introduce delays.

name: Resource Contention
description: If the servers are competing for the same resources (e.g., CPU cores, memory), this can create bottlenecks during the coin flip process.

name: Concurrency Control
description: The way concurrency control is implemented (e.g., lock/unlock times) can impact the efficiency of the consensus process.

name: System State
description: The overall state of the system, including the current state of the coin counter and the status of the servers, can influence the latency.

name: Data Volume
description: The volume of data being processed can introduce delays if the consensus process is not efficiently handling it.
